findings.title: A single NaN in continuous hue silently collapses the entire color mapping to 2 colors
findings.description: mat2colors (hypertools/plot/colors.py:58) computes bin edges with np.min/np.max, which return NaN when any hue value is NaN; every edge becomes NaN, np.digitize then sends all numeric values to one clipped bin and NaN values to the other. Result: with hue=[0..59] plus ONE NaN, all 59 informative values render in a single color (plot conveys nothing) with no error and no warning, on every palette. Missing values are ubiquitous in scientific data (the plot_hue / plot_multicolored_lines / plot_colorbar examples all advertise continuous hue for behavioral variables), so this is a realistic silent-wrong-visual. Should either raise a ValueError naming hue/NaN, warn, or bin on nanmin/nanmax with a distinct 'missing' color.
findings.repro:
import os; os.environ['MPLBACKEND']='Agg'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt, hypertools as hyp
d = np.random.default_rng(1).standard_normal((60, 4)).cumsum(axis=0)
hue = np.arange(60.0); hue[7] = np.nan
fig = hyp.plot(d, fmt='.', hue=hue, ndims=2, palette='viridis')
fig.canvas.draw()
fc = np.vstack([c.get_facecolors() for c in fig.axes[0].collections])
print(np.unique(np.round(fc, 5), axis=0).shape[0])  # -> 2 (60 without the NaN)
findings.expected: Either an informative ValueError/warning about NaN in hue, or NaN-aware binning (nanmin/nanmax edges + sentinel color) so the 59 valid values keep their 60-color gradient.
findings.actual:
palette=viridis: unique colors clean=60  with-1-NaN=2
   COLLAPSED example colors: [[0.27, 0.015, 0.341, 1.0], [0.974, 0.904, 0.13, 1.0]]
palette=hls: unique colors clean=60  with-1-NaN=2  (no warning, no error)

findings.title: plot_hue.py emits 900 NumPy DeprecationWarnings and uses an unseeded RNG
findings.description: examples/plot_hue.py line 31 does `int(np.random.randint(1000, size=1))` inside a loop over all 900 observations (3 datasets x 300 rows). Under numpy 2.3.5 each call raises 'DeprecationWarning: Conversion of an array with ndim > 0 to a scalar is deprecated, and will error in future. (Deprecated NumPy 1.25.)' -- 900 warnings per run, and the example will hard-CRASH on a future numpy. Also np.random is unseeded, so the gallery figure changes on every docs build. Fix: `int(np.random.randint(1000))` (or a seeded default_rng + vectorized draw).

findings.title: df2mat relies on deprecated pandas-3 compat: select_dtypes(['object']) no longer matches str columns (Pandas4Warning on the basic DataFrame example)
findings.description: Running examples/plot_dataframe.py under pandas 3.0.3 emits 'Pandas4Warning: For backward compatibility, 'str' dtypes are included by select_dtypes when 'object' dtype is specified. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a future version.' from hypertools/tools/df2mat.py:32. Under pandas 3's string migration, text columns are 'str' dtype, not 'object'; df2mat only works today via a temporary compat shim. When pandas 4 removes it, df_str becomes empty, text columns fall into df_num, and .values yields a str/object matrix that crashes reduce/normalize -- i.e. every text DataFrame input (including the mushrooms example) breaks. Fix: select_dtypes(include=['object', 'str']) / exclude same.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python examples/plot_dataframe.py  # observe Pandas4Warning from df2mat.py:32
findings.expected: No deprecation warning; dummy-coding keyed on both 'object' and 'str' dtypes so behavior survives pandas 4.
findings.actual: Pandas4Warning: For backward compatibility, 'str' dtypes are included by select_dtypes when 'object' dtype is specified. This behavior is deprecated and will be removed in a future version. ... [df2mat.py:32]

findings.title: labels= length mismatch raises bare 'IndexError: list index out of range' instead of an informative ValueError
findings.description: hyp.plot(data, labels=<too-short list>) crashes in matplotlib_backend.py:538 (annotate_plot: 'if labels[idx] is not None') with a bare IndexError -- no kwarg name, no expected/actual counts, no fix. This is inconsistent with sibling kwargs: hue, legend/label, rotations, chemtrails and label_alpha all raise rich ValueErrors naming counts (the chemtrails docstring even advertises 'naming both counts'). The labels docstring says it 'must be a list the length of the number of datapoints' so a length check at validation time is expected. findings.title: Default palette for continuous hue is circular (hls): minimum and maximum hue values render visually identical
findings.description: Continuous hue is binned through the default 'hls' palette, which is a closed hue circle: bin 0 color (0.86, 0.371, 0.34) vs bin 99 color (0.86, 0.34, 0.34), L2 distance 0.031 (viridis endpoints: 1.15). Consequence, visible in the shipped gallery figures: in plot_multicolored_lines a trajectory 'colored by time' starts and ends in the same red, and in plot_colorbar fig1 the colorbar's 0.0 and 1.0 ends are indistinguishable -- a reader cannot tell min from max anywhere the color wraps. A perceptually ordered default colormap for CONTINUOUS hue (e.g. viridis, keeping hls for categorical) or a docstring warning would fix it.
findings.repro: MPLBACKEND=Agg /Users/jmanning/hypertools/.venv/bin/python -c "import numpy as np; from hypertools.plot.colors import mat2colors; c = mat2colors(np.arange(100.0), palette='hls'); print(np.round(c[0],3), np.round(c[-1],3), np.linalg.norm(c[0]-c[-1]))"
findings.expected: Endpoints of a continuous color scale clearly distinguishable (monotone perceptual colormap).
findings.actual: hls endpoint colors: first [0.86, 0.371, 0.34] last [0.86, 0.34, 0.34] | L2 dist: 0.0312

findings.title: morph_samples=-5 leaks a numpy internal error ('negative dimensions are not allowed')
findings.description: hyp.plot([a, b], animate='morph', morph_samples=-5) raises 'ValueError: negative dimensions are not allowed' from numpy's RNG during downsampling -- the kwarg is never named and the message gives no fix, unlike the polished rotations/chemtrails/label_alpha validation nearby. morph_samples docstring (plot.py ~887) documents 'int or None' with no validation promise, so a simple '>= 1' check with a named error would close the gap.

findings.title: legend= list length mismatch error names 'label=' instead of the kwarg the user passed
findings.description: hyp.plot(three_datasets, legend=['A', 'B']) raises "ValueError: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 2, but there are 3 dataset(s) to plot...". The counts and fix are excellent, but the user passed legend=, not label=; plot.py's own style-kwargs docstring promises the error 'nam[es] the kwarg'. Internally legend lists are rerouted through the label broadcast machinery; the error should keep the user-facing name.
findings.repro:
import os; os.environ['MPLBACKEND']='Agg'
import numpy as np, matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
import hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
hyp.plot([rng.standard_normal((40, 4)) for _ in range(3)], fmt='.', legend=['A', 'B'])
findings.expected: Error text mentioning legend= (the kwarg actually supplied).
findings.actual: ValueError: label= was given as a list/tuple of length 2, but there are 3 dataset(s) to plot; pass either a single value (broadcast to every dataset) or a list/tuple of length 3.
